A hawkish pause: the FOMC holds the target range at 5.25–5.50% and continues balance-sheet runoff, emphasizing cumulative tightening and policy lags—an approach consistent with Taylor-rule guidance when inflation remains above target and with the caution advocated in the real-time policy literature (e.g., Orphanides). The acknowledgement that tighter credit will weigh on activity reflects the Bernanke–Gertler credit channel/financial accelerator, while noting a “sound and resilient” banking system tempers systemic risk concerns. The focus on inflation expectations aligns with New Keynesian frameworks (Woodford; Mankiw–Reis sticky information), reinforcing commitment to the 2% target. Net tone is slightly negative for growth and risk assets but balanced by easing inflation and financial resilience.
